reviews.rationale: The module sequences one knowledge migration lifecycle; formatting, bootstrap application, and top-level dispatch are extracted, while the remaining effects share ordered plan, approval, rollback, and event contracts.

Move, merge, split, and delete are variants of one exact-approved document-structure command contract and share the same validation, normalization-relocation reporting, materialization event, and rollback boundary.

All functions validate or execute one managed deliberation lifecycle and share the same provider plan, writing contract, checkpoint, and interruption semantics. Participant route validation, verified role composition, and organization-event mutation are isolated in the deliberation participant binding module; this module only orders binding, round execution, terminal release, and the existing lifecycle boundaries.
The module owns one read-only selection adapter lifecycle; pure projection and authorization, durable record construction, and managed-run composition remain in separate modules.

The CLI composes one managed run from admission through writing publication and finalization. Research source capture and checker environment validation are delegated to dedicated CLI adapters; the entrypoint adds only ordered preparation and port coordinates. Capability, skill, provider and storage policies remain behind their existing boundaries.

The module owns the immutable v1 base route catalog and composes additive protocol upgrades. Version-specific v4 through v11 additions remain in dedicated modules; command parsing, product inspection, projection policy, and rendering are separate. Its length is declarative catalog data rather than mixed execution responsibility.

Argument parsing, inspection, exact role-approval validation, stage application, lint, and receipt formatting all describe one bounded repository-upgrade command lifecycle and share one outer plan identity; workforce policy and persistence remain in their owning package.

TLS material loading, dependency and server composition, reload, resource lifecycle orchestration, and health wiring are phases of one Hub deployment boundary; HTTP connection-drain mechanics and domain policy remain in linked modules.

The module composes one provider-neutral supervision runtime from storage, admission, reasoning, execution, and evidence ports. Request-origin evaluation, resource policy, provider effects, supersession, leases, and snapshot projection remain in dedicated modules; this boundary only wires their ordered lifecycle and cleanup.

The class owns one external Claude protocol boundary and translates native session, tool, telemetry, stop, and result behavior into common adapter contracts; the accounting declaration remains in a linked descriptor module. The explicit login profile is snapshotted for this same provider-session lifecycle; environment construction and native process transport remain separate modules.

The class owns the Codex provider boundary, selects one injected native transport, and translates thread, turn, telemetry, stop, and result behavior into common adapter contracts; transport parsing and the accounting declaration remain linked modules. The explicit login profile is snapshotted for this same provider-session lifecycle; environment construction and native process transport remain separate modules.

The module executes one provider-neutral adapter conformance lifecycle from descriptor and session start through context, turn, telemetry, result identity, and stop; provider translation and focused binding rules remain in linked modules.

Read-only planning, per-role approval binding, and atomic agent or assignment transitions are phases of one workforce migration lifecycle; role resolution, capability resolution, state storage, event schemas, and CLI presentation remain behind linked package boundaries.

The module declaratively owns backward-compatible capability-report, route, and result-contract types from v1 through v11. Runtime composition, command parsing, product projection, persistence, and rendering remain in separate modules; its length follows the explicit versioned compatibility history rather than mixed implementation concerns.

The repository class owns one SQLite persistence boundary for platform bindings, including validation, reads, writes, and transaction-safe state changes. Inbound depth and the optional ordered active-target projection use only identities resolved at that same mapping boundary; participation, discussion scheduling, and turn ownership policy remain outside the adapter.

The module owns one in-memory deliberation state machine; artifact publication failure recording, handoff materialization, snapshot restoration, and event recording remain in linked modules, while methods enforce shared history and event invariants. The optional policy-role name is validated once and recorded as provider-neutral event metadata without adding surface rendering or transport behavior.

The module owns one pure event-payload privacy boundary: its large declarative allowlist, schema dispatch, and coordinate checks produce one sanitized result without I/O. Assignment access-mode and knowledge-job validators are separate. Prompts, source bytes, paths, credentials, and provider output remain excluded; schemas and persistence stay in separate modules.
The declarative migration catalog and migration runner own one versioned SQLite schema boundary; length is driven by schema history rather than mixed runtime policy.

One SQLite adapter composes repositories under the shared database, transaction, and schema lifecycle. Notification retention and waiting live in a separate adapter; this facade emits only committed scope coordinates and closes notifications with the store.
Read, lint, query, export, import, and re-export are operations over one external OKF format boundary with shared safety, trust, and byte-preservation rules.

The coordinator owns one provider-neutral run lifecycle and failure ledger. Role input binding, provider-interaction limits, snapshots, result collection, and verification remain delegated to dedicated modules and ports; the coordinator only orders them and records their evidence. No research, filesystem source policy, checker process, or provider-specific behavior is introduced here.

Reservation, completion, recovery projection, target binding, and integrity checks all operate on one immutable rollback replay table and transaction lifecycle; authorization and rollback policy remain outside the adapter.
The class owns one SQLite policy persistence boundary and its approval, verification, transaction, and query operations.

Process control plus Codex and Claude response and usage parsing implement one capability-free provider boundary for typed JSON, semantic compilation, and document normalization contracts; resource admission remains in repository knowledge.
Publication rendering, desired output construction, recorded-output comparison, and plan creation are phases of one deterministic structural compilation contract.

Profiles, envelopes, candidate validation, lifecycle inspection, generation orchestration, candidate storage, planning, and exact-approved apply share one content-bound lifecycle. Observation policy, explicit selection and workset/preflight contracts, shard-cache storage, and CLI parsing or rendering are separate modules.
Plan serialization, safe source inspection, merge planning, lineage updates, and apply are one atomic document-merge responsibility.

Destination safety, plan serialization, lineage, single-output normalization-record preservation, plan creation, and apply are one atomic document-move responsibility; normalization record mechanics remain in a separate bounded module and formatter configuration is outside this transaction.
Heading extraction, destination safety, plan serialization, lineage preservation, and apply are one atomic document-split responsibility.
Journal creation, binding checks, safe writes, rollback, recovery, and cleanup implement one atomic filesystem transaction protocol.
Profile resolution, registry binding, structural refresh, plan creation, and exact-approved apply share one instruction-bridge lifecycle; target construction and classification are extracted.
Query behavior and safe publication access were extracted; the remaining functions exclusively validate manifests, layout, normalization, lineage, and semantic sidecars.
Coordinate extraction, candidate validation, protected-change review, plan creation, and apply implement one byte-safe README improvement contract.
Policy validation, review identity, disposition validation, artifact persistence, and event recording form one exact-review responsibility.
Existing registry inspection, candidate signatures, conflict options, and dispositions jointly produce one read-only reconciliation plan.

Classification, link rebasing, neutral ownership-record migration, machine moves, user updates, serialization, plan creation, and apply are phases of one repository-wide layout transaction; tool-specific formatter configuration is outside this boundary.

Classification, safe reads, transient-cache exclusion, source-unit extraction, scan construction, and immutable scan transforms all own the canonical scanned-source aggregate. The shared cache-name decision remains outside this filesystem scanner; no independent transport or provider concern was added.
Compilation identity, bounded sharding, provider response validation, and candidate assembly are phases of one semantic compiler contract.
Review loading, operation derivation, publication generation, plan creation, and apply share one review-bound materialization contract.
Move, split, and merge lineage creation and validation operate on one lineage schema and safe registry-loading boundary.
Provider configuration merge, runtime integrity, inspection, plan creation, and apply form one fail-closed terminal integration contract.
The module exposes one package-level contract surface for repository scans, plans, operations, lifecycle results, diagnostics, and typed domain failures without owning their implementations.

Current state, continuation import, start, update, and replicated import preserve one WorkstreamSnapshot aggregate, exact origin and predecessor invariants, CAS binding, and durable apply protocol. Pure snapshot construction and pending-coordinate validation now live in workstream-snapshot.ts, so this module retains durable lifecycle orchestration rather than growing another policy concern.
Identity calculation, registry validation, service-file inspection, onboarding planning, listing, and registration share one owner-only fleet registry contract.
The file is a declarative schema catalog for one adapter protocol; its length is data-shaped and contains no independent executable workflow.

The module contains only bounded JSON Schema declarations and inferred payload types for one organization-agent event catalog. Version-two deliberation participation fields extend the existing bound event additively; projection, privacy redaction, persistence, and execution remain in separate modules.

The module contains only the bounded JSON Schema declarations and inferred payload types for one terminal observation lifecycle; runtime validation, redaction, persistence, and orchestration remain in their owning modules.

This module registers compiled validators for the schema catalog. The conversation knowledge outcome adds only a linked declarative validator; schema definitions, domain decisions, configuration handling, and persistence remain in their owning modules. No runtime workflow policy is added.
Case validation, paired timing, quality aggregation, latency statistics, environment capture, and reporting form one reproducible benchmark protocol.

Dependency inventory, manifest, SBOM, archive, platform validation, and verification are phases of one Node distribution artifact contract. Generic mode-preserving tar extraction is delegated to the shared archive boundary.

The module verifies one ordered, additive external-consumer protocol catalog from v1 through v11. It contains bounded expected descriptors only; repository journeys, product projection behavior, packaging, and release orchestration remain in separate scripts and focused tests.
Temporary project setup, process control, HTTPS calls, event observation, assertions, and cleanup compose one end-to-end acceptance scenario; command invocation is a separate thin entrypoint.

The touched orchestration composes isolated supervision and work-admission guards around one exact service transaction. Status stabilization, activation, compensation and rollback share the same manager-state recovery policy; presentation and process exit remain outside. Existing argument and source validation are bounded to this transaction's exact inputs.

The module composes the bounded suite, isolated workspaces, provider-neutral evidence selection, paired arm schedule, and cleanup; command invocation, versioned acceptance, report evaluation, provider preparation and transports, and selection policy remain separate.

The module owns one immutable comparison-contract lineage: protocols, schema, suite validation, and pure acceptance evaluation share the same version and gate lifecycle, while provider execution and evidence selection remain separate.

The module declaratively validates one lineage of recent immutable canary checkpoints; preparation, execution, storage, and reporting remain in separate modules, while the length follows explicit version-bound predecessor evidence.

The module composes and validates one lineage of immutable provider-shadow contracts; policy, preparation I/O, execution, observation, and review remain in separate modules, while the length follows explicit historical contract variants.
